acceptanceCriteria: A pool declares any subset of the five operations, and an undeclared one is refused with a typed reason.
An operation in an illegal member state is refused with a typed reason, and nothing runs.
Each run records operation, request id, exit class and output digest; `pool status` shows the last receipt per operation.
The same request id replays the recorded outcome and never runs twice.
A failed retarget or reset leaves the member QUARANTINED with the operation named in the reason.
Timeouts kill the whole process group, and output is bounded as for existing commands.
Pools that do not use the new fields behave as before.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1028 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem A pool member that is a disposable test environment needs more than health/cleanup/safeReuse/prepare. It must be built from a pinned source, refreshed without losing data, reset to a clean template, moved to another allowed source, and torn down. The queue knows none of this; it only knows FREE, QUARANTINED and HELD. It cannot tell which operations a member has had, cannot refuse an operation while another holder is active, and cannot show what a member currently serves. Current workaround A separate CLI keeps a private marker per environment, and wrapper scripts decide which operation to run after each release. The queue sees only opaque commands, so a failed rebuild leaves the member in an unknown state that scripts must probe. Proposal Extend memberConfig with optional named operations `provision`, `refresh`, `reset`, `retarget` and `teardown`, using the existing command shape See beamfall/corvint#1028 for the full text.
title: pool: typed member lifecycle operations (provision, refresh, reset, retarget, teardown) with recorded outcomes (issue #1028)
